The orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Therefore, we get the following projection: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}6 & 6 \\ 6 & 9\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}8 \\ 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & -\frac{1}{3} \\ -\frac{1}{3} & \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}8 \\ 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3} \\ \frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

The acute angle between $x$ and $S$ is the acute angle between $x$ and ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$   

Computing the cosine using the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{x\cdot {\text{proj}}_{S}x}{‖x‖‖{\text{proj}}_{S}x‖} \\  & =\frac{3\cdot 2+2\cdot 2+1\cdot 2}{\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{12}{\sqrt{14}\sqrt{12}} \\  & =\frac{12}{2\sqrt{42}} \\  & =\frac{6}{\sqrt{42}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, 

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{6}{\sqrt{42}})≈{22.21}^{∘},
$$

which is already an acute angle.

In our case, we have A=[||a1a2||]=[122112]⟹AT=[121212].

Therefore, we get the following projection:

projSx=[122112]⋅([121212]⋅[122112])−1⋅[121212]⋅[321]=[122112]⋅[6669]−1⋅[810]=[122112]⋅[12−13−1313]⋅[810]=[122112]⋅[2323]=[222].

The acute angle between x and S is the acute angle between x and projSx.

Computing the cosine using the dot product, we obtain

cos⁡θ=x⋅projSx‖x‖‖projSx‖=3⋅2+2⋅2+1⋅232+22+12⋅22+22+22=121412=12242=642

Therefore,

θ=arccos⁡(642)≈22.21∘,

which is already an acute angle.
